topic: Robust joint-intervention design on locally switched causal stars. Fix binary observed variables with arrows w→T for every proxy w and T→Y, and let independent two-mode local switches choose bidirected edges, with equality/complement copies only. Before switch modes are revealed, choose one unit-cost proxy set J and acquire the complete single joint source P(V\J | do(J=j)) for every j, plus P(V). Prove P_t(Y) is identifiable on a completion iff T and Y are disconnected after deleting J; give the explicit adjustment functional and strictly positive binary same-source countermodels when a path survives. Prove deciding whether some |J|≤B works for every completion is Σ₂ᴾ-complete using occurrence-copy pairs, budget-saturating pair tests, consistency paths, and selector-isolated clause chains, with singleton T,Y, constant-size switches, and nonterminal bidirected degree at most eight; return J and per-completion gID certificates or, for a fixed failing J, a completion and hedge. Compare explicitly with Akbari et al. 2023/2025, Elahi et al. 2024, Jaber et al. 2022, and switched robust-cut literature. The consumer is a dosearch pre-data design mode for one multiplex intervention under local graph uncertainty. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: The presolve derived the exact causal-star disconnect criterion, adjustment formula, and full-support binary indistinguishability construction. It built a quantified reduction whose rounding argument prevents auxiliary interventions and whose selector chains prevent inactive-module bypasses. Exact checks matched hedge and path criteria in 8,192 graph/intervention cases, exhausted all budget-feasible cuts in four compiled quantified examples, and verified dyadic countermodel tables for one-to-four internal proxies. Greatest-completion families collapse to ordinary cut; bounded possible terminal neighborhoods and PAG scope are excluded, and terminal degrees remain unbounded. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently audit the uniform occurrence/equality/selector compiler and resolve priority against switched-cut and forbidden-pair-path literature; do not broaden from the proved causal-star criterion to unrestricted strictly-binary gID without a separate semantic completeness proof. EARLY KILL TEST: Regenerate every two-clause formula over one existential and one universal variable, exhaust all auxiliary-inclusive budget cuts and switch assignments, and stop if quantified truth ever differs from residual T–Y disconnection. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_robust_jointdo_qbf.md.

open_problems.open_problem: For a binary causal star with independently switched equality/complement bidirected-edge modules, characterize exactly when one ex ante joint proxy intervention J makes P_t(Y) identifiable from P(V) and {P(V\J | do(J=j)) : j}, uniformly over every switch completion.

source_refs.claim: Studies probabilistic edge uncertainty but optimizes for a most-plausible identifiable subgraph rather than choosing one experiment valid for every completion.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Fateme Jamshidi, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Matthew J. Vowels, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Gives a sound-and-complete gID algorithm under positivity by reducing a fixed-graph gID instance to classical identification subproblems.
source_refs.author: Yaroslav Kivva, Ehsan Mokhtarian, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Designs low-cost proxy experiments for a specified effect in one known ADMG and separately studies designs that yield valid adjustment sets.
source_refs.author: Sepehr Elahi, Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash, Patrick Thiran

open_problems.why_unsolved: Kivva et al. treat one fixed ADMG and fixed input distributions; Elahi et al. optimize experiments for one known ADMG; and Akbari et al. optimize an identifiable subgraph under probabilistic edge uncertainty. None supplies one identifying functional valid across a succinct family with correlated equality/complement edge choices. The unverified presolve claim therefore still requires an independent semantic audit: fixed-completion hedge elimination must be shown to collapse to T–Y disconnection after deleting J, and every surviving path must yield strictly positive models agreeing on the same observational and multiplex-intervention sources.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An independently verified iff characterization equating uniform identification with T–Y disconnection after deleting J, an explicit completion-invariant adjustment functional, and full-support binary same-source countermodels for every surviving-path regime.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation makes fragility to graph misspecification the central problem before introducing a formal uncertainty model.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Classical ID assumes one correct graph -> edge uncertainty makes graph-conditional conclusions fragile -> existing work optimizes over plausible identifiable subgraphs -> robust pre-data design instead needs one proxy source valid for every local-switch completion

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce positive-distribution gID to classical fixed-graph identification subproblems and organize nonidentifiability through their failure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Every switch completion is a positive fixed-graph gID instance, while the proposed characterization must prove that all instances share one disconnection criterion and functional.

method_exemplars.technique: Use hedgelets and thickets to prove necessity and construct identifying expressions from arbitrary surrogate experiments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Surviving-path countermodels are restricted-family analogues of gID failure witnesses, and the multiplex intervention is a surrogate experiment.

method_exemplars.technique: Rewrite gID expressions as generalized multi-outcome sequential back-door functionals, then derive multiply robust estimators and asymptotic convergence results.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Once established, the star functional combines observational and experimental sources in the same structural form.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the exact complexity of deciding whether some unit-cost proxy set J with |J|≤B identifies P_t(Y) for every completion of a succinct family of independent two-mode local switches, under singleton T,Y, constant-size switches, and bounded nonterminal bidirected degree.

source_refs.claim: For one known semi-Markovian graph, minimum-cost intervention design is NP-complete, is equivalent to hitting relevant hedges, and is logarithmically hard to approximate.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Reformulates fixed-graph minimum-cost proxy experiment design as weighted Max-SAT and ILP using an encoding of hedge-hull reachability.
source_refs.author: Sepehr Elahi, Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash, Patrick Thiran

source_refs.claim: Proves Separating by Forbidden Pairs Σ₂ᴾ-complete even on acyclic graphs; its selected arc pairs must jointly intersect every s–t path.
source_refs.author: Oliver Bachtler, Tim Bergner, Sven O. Krumke

open_problems.why_unsolved: Known-graph causal experiment design has an existential NP structure because identification for a proposed design is polynomially checkable. Local-switch uncertainty adds a universal completion quantifier resembling Separating by Forbidden Pairs, but that problem selects arc pairs rather than causal intervention vertices. The unverified compiler must preserve causal-star semantics, enforce consistent choices across occurrence copies, prevent budget expenditure on auxiliary vertices, and exclude inactive selector-module bypasses while retaining constant switches and bounded nonterminal degree.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An independently audited polynomial many-one reduction from QSAT₂ and a matching Σ₂ᴾ-membership proof, with a formal correspondence between satisfying existential assignments and budget-feasible proxy sets and exhaustive agreement on the stated early-kill instances.

writing_exemplar.why: It moves from infeasible direct experiments to proxy design and then translates the causal obstruction into solver-ready combinatorics.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Direct intervention is costly or infeasible -> proxy experiments may identify the target -> selecting proxies is hard even for one graph -> choosing one proxy set against every switched completion creates quantified complexity

method_exemplars.technique: Encode existential forbidden-pair selection followed by a universal obstruction over all s–t paths and prove Σ₂ᴾ-hardness from quantified satisfiability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After reducing star identification to disconnection, robust proxy design has the same existential-design/universal-surviving-path skeleton.

method_exemplars.technique: Represent hedge-hull reachability iterations by Boolean variables and clauses, then couple intervention costs to a weighted Max-SAT instance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates how to preserve causal hedge semantics inside a Boolean compiler, to which switch and consistency gadgets must be added.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce intervention design to hitting every relevant hedge and prove both directions between combinatorial covers and causal obstruction destruction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The robust reduction must similarly connect each selected proxy set to elimination of every completion-specific obstruction.

open_problems.open_problem: Can a dosearch-style pre-data planner over a succinct local-switch family return either a proxy set J with compact uniform gID certificates or, for a fixed failing J, one completion and a hedge without explicitly enumerating all switch completions?

source_refs.claim: Provides a sound-and-complete gID procedure for arbitrary observational and experimental inputs, with structured non-gID witnesses, on a fixed graph.
source_refs.author: Sanghack Lee, Juan D. Correa, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Gives a sound-and-complete calculus and algorithm for conditional-effect identification from a PAG representing one Markov-equivalence class.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Adèle H. Ribeiro, Jiji Zhang, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Uses SAT and ILP formulations to avoid explicitly enumerating exponentially many minimal hedges in a fixed graph.
source_refs.author: Sepehr Elahi, Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash, Patrick Thiran

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fixed-graph gID algorithms emit a functional or a fixed-graph obstruction, while PAG calculus exploits invariances within one equivalence class. A local equality/complement switch circuit is generally not a PAG because superposing possible edges discards correlations between edge choices. Running gID independently on all completions gives exponential work or output. What is missing is a switch-aware certificate language whose verifier respects those correlations and whose negative certificates expose one concrete completion and obstruction.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sound-and-complete certifying algorithm with explicit polynomially checkable certificate syntax and size bounds, returning J plus a symbolic uniform derivation, or returning a switch assignment and checkable hedge whenever a fixed J fails.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents identification as a decision-and-construction problem in which both successful formulas and rigorous failure witnesses matter.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Data arise from arbitrary experiments -> graphical ID must decide whether the sources suffice -> completeness requires formulas and failure witnesses -> succinct graph families need the same two-sided interface without completion enumeration

method_exemplars.technique: Produce identifying expressions recursively while using hedgelets and thickets as structured failure witnesses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These are the fixed-completion proof objects that a switch-aware uniform certificate must compress or index.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift graphical-calculus rules from individual diagrams to a partially specified graph and prove algorithmic completeness.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The target also needs rules valid across a graph family, although switch correlations require a representation richer than a PAG.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode reachability iterations and hedge-hull emptiness in polynomial-size SAT and ILP formulations.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A switch-aware extension could represent completion checks symbolically while retaining extractable positive and negative certificates.

open_problems.open_problem: Does robust joint-proxy design on local-switch causal stars remain Σ₂ᴾ-complete when the bidirected degrees of both terminals T and Y are bounded by a fixed constant, or does bounded terminal neighborhood yield a polynomial-time or fixed-parameter algorithm?

source_refs.claim: Shows tractable fixed-graph intervention-design cases for tree-like directed/bidirected structure and restricted hedge families, demonstrating that structural restrictions can collapse complexity.
source_refs.author: Sina Akbari, Jalal Etesami, Negar Kiyavash

source_refs.claim: Establishes Σ₂ᴾ-hardness for Separating by Forbidden Pairs on acyclic graphs, but does not supply the bounded source/sink incidence required by the causal terminal restriction.
source_refs.author: Oliver Bachtler, Tim Bergner, Sven O. Krumke

open_problems.why_unsolved: The current unverified causal compiler permits unbounded terminal degree, while known fixed-graph results show that structural restrictions can make intervention design tractable. The closest quantified path-separation hardness theorem preserves acyclicity but not bounded incidence at the two terminals. Standard reductions route many variable or clause chains through common terminals, so degree reduction must replace those hubs without breaking the single budget, equality/complement switching, or the correspondence between universal assignments and residual T–Y paths.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either a bounded-terminal-degree Σ₂ᴾ-hardness reduction preserving constant switches and bounded nonterminal degree, or an algorithm with running time f(d,k)poly(n), accompanied by a matching lower bound where possible, parameterized by terminal degree d and switch-interface width k.

writing_exemplar.why: Its complexity narrative pairs general hardness with sharply stated tractable graph and hedge subclasses, which is the appropriate framing for a terminal-degree frontier.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: General proxy design is hard -> graph structure can make hedge covering tractable -> local-switch robustness adds a universal layer -> determine whether bounded terminal neighborhoods restore tractability or preserve quantified hardness

method_exemplars.technique: Exploit restricted directed and bidirected path structure to construct hedge closures and solve the induced covering problem efficiently.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Bounded terminal interfaces may constrain the overlap of completion-specific T–Y paths sufficiently for dynamic programming over switch boundaries.

method_exemplars.technique: Use a quantified-satisfiability reduction whose universal obstruction is an s–t path avoiding all selected forbidden pairs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A hardness resolution must degree-reduce this quantified path skeleton while preserving assignment consistency.

open_problems.open_problem: For a proxy set J that uniformly identifies the star target, derive semiparametrically efficient estimation and confidence intervals from finite observational and complete joint-intervention samples, uniformly over the local-switch completion family under quantitative positivity.

source_refs.claim: Constructs multiply robust estimators and asymptotic convergence theory for g-identifiable functionals from fixed combinations of observational and experimental distributions.
source_refs.author: Yonghan Jung, Iván Díaz, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Develops identification conditions and robust estimators for joint treatment effects assembled from multiple marginal experiments under positivity.
source_refs.author: Yonghan Jung, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

source_refs.claim: Derives influence-function and double-machine-learning estimators for causal effects invariant over a PAG, but uses observational data rather than an ex ante multiplex experimental source.
source_refs.author: Yonghan Jung, Jin Tian, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest gID estimators assume a fixed graph and identifying expression, while PAG-based DML handles one equivalence-class representation using observational data. Uniform inference for a design chosen before switch revelation additionally requires a quantitative positivity envelope, a completion-invariant tangent-space calculation, and uniform control of nuisance-product remainders over the switch family. The located estimation papers do not give an efficiency bound or honest confidence theorem for this pre-data robust multiplex design.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An efficient influence function for the completion-invariant adjustment functional, a cross-fitted estimator attaining its efficiency bound, and a root-n uniform CLT with consistently estimable variance over all allowed completions and distributions satisfying a stated positivity margin.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames effect estimation as an end-to-end problem when the exact causal graph is unavailable and the target must remain invariant across structural alternatives.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: The exact graph is rarely known -> an effect may nevertheless be invariant across candidate structures -> identification alone does not provide finite-sample uncertainty -> robust multiplex design needs inference valid for every switch completion

method_exemplars.technique: Rewrite gID functionals as generalized multi-outcome sequential back-door adjustments, derive influence-function-based multiply robust estimators, and prove convergence under nuisance-rate conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The star target is a low-dimensional gID functional of one observational and one multiplex experimental source.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine experimental samples through regression, weighting, and cross-fitted doubly robust scores under explicit cross-source positivity conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required estimator similarly combines cells indexed by joint intervention values while keeping source-specific nuisance functions and variance terms explicit.

method_exemplars.technique: Derive an influence function for a causal effect invariant across a PAG and construct a double/debiased machine-learning estimator.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest frequentist template for causal estimation valid across multiple graph possibilities rather than conditional on one fully specified graph.

literature_map:
Akbari, Etesami, and Kiyavash (JMLR 2025; arXiv:2205.02232) establish NP-completeness and logarithmic inapproximability for minimum-cost effect-identifying interventions in one known ADMG, with tractable structured cases.
Elahi et al. (NeurIPS 2024; arXiv:2407.05330) replace explicit minimal-hedge enumeration by weighted-Max-SAT and ILP reachability encodings and separately study adjustment-based proxy designs.
Akbari et al. (NeurIPS 2023; arXiv:2208.04627) model uncertain edge existence probabilistically and seek a most-plausible identifiable subgraph, not adversarial ex ante design over all completions.
Bareinboim and Pearl (UAI 2012; arXiv:1210.4842) provide the foundational z-identification criterion and complete algorithm for experiments on manipulable proxies.
Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (UAI 2020) formulate gID for arbitrary surrogate experiments and use hedgelets and thickets for positive and negative identification results.
Kivva et al. (UAI 2022; arXiv:2206.01081) identify the positivity issue in earlier gID formulations and give a corrected sound-and-complete reduction to classical ID subproblems.
Lee and Shpitser (arXiv:2004.01157) treat arbitrary marginal and conditional interventional inputs through SWIGs and nested factorization, with completeness for ancestral-marginal inputs.
Jaber et al. (NeurIPS 2022; DOI:10.52202/068431-0266) give complete conditional-effect identification for a PAG, but a PAG does not preserve arbitrary equality/complement correlations among optional edges.
Recent robust-ID work over candidate equivalence classes supplies sufficient cross-graph criteria, reinforcing that completeness for richer correlated graph families remains delicate.
Jung, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2021) construct influence-function and DML estimators for effects invariant over a PAG.
Jung, Díaz, Tian, and Bareinboim (NeurIPS 2023) extend multiply robust estimation to causal effects identifiable from combined observational and experimental sources.
Jung, Tian, and Bareinboim (ICML 2023) identify and estimate joint treatment effects from multiple marginal experiments, providing a nearby finite-sample analogue to multiplex intervention cells.
Bachtler, Bergner, and Krumke (TCS 2024; arXiv:2202.10090) prove Separating by Forbidden Pairs Σ₂ᴾ-complete even on acyclic graphs, matching the existential-design/universal-path quantifier pattern.
Rebennack, Prokopyev, and Singh (Networks 2020; DOI:10.1002/net.21922) show that two-stage stochastic s–t cut loses total unimodularity and is NP-hard generally but tractable on trees; its scenario and recourse semantics differ from fixed ex ante local switching.
The principal unoccupied intersection is one preselected joint proxy source, a succinct correlated local-switch ADMG family, a completion-uniform functional and witness theorem, and quantified certification suitable for dosearch.
